relevance_reason: This paper identifies loss-of-function mutations in SPECC1L as the cause of oblique facial clefting and adds functional and animal-model evidence.

findings.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) showed that loss-of-function mutations in the SPECC1L gene are pathogenic for oblique facial clefts (ObFC), a unique class of facial malformations.
quotes: We show that loss-of-function mutations in SPECC1L are pathogenic for this human developmental disorder and that SPECC1L is a critical organizer of vertebrate facial morphogenesis.

findings.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that knockdown of a SPECC1L homolog in zebrafish produced a faceless phenotype with loss of jaw and facial structures. In Drosophila, knockdown phenocopied mutants in the integrin signaling pathway, which have cell-migration and cell-adhesion defects.
quotes: In zebrafish, knockdown of a SPECC1L homolog produces a faceless phenotype with loss of jaw and facial structures, and knockdown in Drosophila phenocopies mutants in the integrin signaling pathway that exhibit cell-migration and -adhesion defects.

findings.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that during mouse embryogenesis, Specc1l is expressed in the cells of the developing facial primordia, which proliferate and fuse to form the face. In mammalian cells, SPECC1L colocalized with both tubulin and actin. SPECC1L deficiency caused defective reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton and abnormal cell adhesion and migration. The authors concluded that SPECC1L functions in actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and is required for proper facial morphogenesis.
quotes: During murine embryogenesis, Specc1l is expressed in cell populations of the developing facial primordial, which proliferate and fuse to form the face.

Furthermore, in mammalian cells, SPECC1L colocalizes with both tubulin and actin, and its deficiency results in defective actin-cytoskeleton reorganization, as well as abnormal cell adhesion and migration.
Collectively, these data demonstrate that SPECC1L functions in actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and is required for proper facial morphogenesis.

relevance_reason: The paper is a case series of 4 Brazilian patients with oblique facial clefts. Consanguinity in 3 of them suggests a distinct dysmorphogenetic process, possibly an oculomaxillofacial dysostosis.

findings.statement: Richieri-Costa and Gorlin (1994) reported 4 Brazilian patients with oblique facial clefts and a strikingly similar facial appearance. Three of them had consanguineous parents. The authors suggested that the pattern of facial involvement and the overall clinical picture pointed to a unique dysmorphogenetic process. In some cases this could represent an oculomaxillofacial dysostosis.
quotes: Here we report on 4 patients with oblique facial clefts and a strikingly similar facial appearance.

The pattern of facial involvement, the presence of consanguinity in 3 of them, as well as the entire clinical picture, suggest a unique dysmorphogenetic process which could represent, in some instances, an oculomaxillofacial dysostosis.

findings.statement: Richieri-Costa and Gorlin (1994) noted that 3 of their 4 Brazilian patients with oblique facial clefts had consanguineous parents. The paper's title cites evidence for clinical variability and genetic heterogeneity.
quotes: the presence of consanguinity in 3 of them
Evidence for clinical variability and genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Richieri-Costa and Gorlin (1994) stated that oblique facial clefts are rare and include types 2 to 6 of Tessier's classification.
quotes: Oblique facial clefts are rare and include types 2-6 of Tessier's classification.

relevance_reason: This case report describes a child with bilateral oblique facial clefts and a de novo balanced t(1;22) translocation. It adds cytogenetic and clinical evidence relevant to oblique facial clefting.

findings.statement: Dasouki et al. (1988) reported an 8-month-old girl born with symmetric bilateral oblique facial clefts and calcaneovarus foot deformity. Head CT showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia and normal brain parenchyma.
quotes: An eight month old girl was born with symmetrical bilateral oblique facial clefts and calcaneovarus foot deformity.
CT scan of the head showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia and normal brain parenchyma.

findings.statement: Dasouki et al. (1988) found a de novo balanced translocation between chromosome 1 and chromosome 22 in the peripheral blood karyotype of a girl with bilateral oblique facial clefts. They noted that a submicroscopic imbalance resulting from the translocation could not be ruled out, and they recommended chromosome studies in children with such rare malformations.
quotes: Peripheral blood karyotype showed a de novo balanced translocation between a chromosome 1 and 22.
A submicroscopic imbalance secondary to this translocation cannot be ruled out.
Chromosomal studies should be performed in children with such rare malformations.

findings.statement: Dasouki et al. (1988) suggested that the pattern of anomalies seen in their patient would help distinguish oblique facial clefts from amniotic band disruption.
quotes: The pattern of the observed anomalies will help distinguish between oblique facial clefts and amniotic band disruption.

relevance_reason: Proposes the anatomical classification of facial and craniofacial clefts (the Tessier numbering) used to describe oblique facial clefts. It reports no specific patients, genes, or variants.

findings.statement: Tessier (1976) proposed an anatomical classification of facial, craniofacial, and laterofacial clefts based on personal observations, using the orbit as the primary structure of reference. Fifteen cleft locations were distinguished, and the course of each through soft tissue and bone was described. Combinations of several cleft types and associated malformations were also discussed.
quotes: Based on personal observations a new classification of facial, cranio-facial and latero-facial clefts is proposed. The orbit is used as the primary structure of reference. Fifteen locations for clefts can be differentiated.
Combinations of several types of clefts and associated malformations are discussed.
